solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One refusing to compromise — sit up angrily, making case for resistance

indicators.note: doing something angrily suggests thrashing about, so the letters of the phrase before it are thrown into disorder
to make a case for something is to wrap around it, so the shuffled letters enclose the following piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A hardliner sits up angrily while making an argument in support of the resistance movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A purist insists on strict correctness and will not accept any watering down of standards.

clue.text: Maybe a surprised expression on second thoughts

blocks.note: 'a' as in 'ten pounds a head' means per
Ha! is an exclamation of surprise
a postscript is an afterthought added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a gasp of surprise might be worth reconsidering.
explanation.walkthrough: PS, the postscript, is how a letter-writer adds second thoughts; 'a' is the per of 'once a week'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs expressing possibility rather than certainty, interchangeable in a sentence.

clue.text: Refuse car trip and come to notice again

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters before it fall out of their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dustcart journey that brings someone back into public view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse car' reads as a bin lorry, and 'trip' as its journey; trip is the shuffle signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that resurfaces reappears or becomes known again after a period out of sight.

clue.text: Not to be commended? Very right, investigator declares at the outset

indicators.note: the outset is the beginning, so only the opening letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: so as an intensifier, as in 'so good'
R is the abbreviation for right
DI is a Detective Inspector
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A detective announces from the start that some conduct deserves no praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: something sordid is hardly praiseworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid behaviour is base and squalid, the opposite of anything one would praise or approve.

clue.text: Hard-working farm promises to pay

blocks.note: a stud is a farm where horses are bred
IOUs are written promises to repay a debt

explanation.surface: A diligent farm that honours its debts.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person applies themselves diligently, especially to study.

clue.text: Change act

blocks.note: first meaning: to become different
second meaning: a performer's slot on stage

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like an instruction to alter behaviour; the two words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to alter as a verb, and a performer's routine as a noun.

clue.text: New ATM card I invested in is effective

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are made over into a different order
money invested in something is put inside it, so this piece goes into the other

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cash card has been put into use and works a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatic effect is striking and impressive, so the word means having a strong impact.

clue.text: Hate element no longer small

indicators.note: the element loses the abbreviation for small, so that one letter drops off

blocks.note: sodium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Someone's loathing for an element of their life has grown.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the standard abbreviation for small, removed from the front of SODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general loathing or opprobrium directed at someone.

clue.text: Have great confidence in son — stand alongside

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to wear is to tolerate or put up with, as in 'he won't wear it'
by means beside

explanation.surface: A parent trusts their son completely and stands by him.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear by something is to rely on it utterly and recommend it.

clue.text: Nice, say, to have fragrant rose, reminder somewhat on reflection

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the phrase is used, lying across its words
a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: A town on the Riviera boasts sweet-smelling roses as a souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective; the capital is hidden by sitting first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is a seaside holiday town on the French Riviera, an example of a resort.

clue.text: Formal work, a pleasure, is close to sublime

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept

blocks.note: a treat is a pleasure
taken as written
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An academic praises a scholarly work as delightful and almost sublime.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a written work dealing systematically and formally with a subject.

clue.text: Glaringly obvious nocturnal type's cornering learner worker

indicators.note: to corner something is to hem it in, so the creature's letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: a bat is a night creature; the 's is 'has'
L is for learner, as on L-plates
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: An obvious night owl is cornering a trainee employee.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'nocturnal type' stands for 'has', which lets the bat contain the learner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blatant is done openly and unashamedly, so it is flagrantly obvious.

clue.text: First-class flier I'd diverted — here?

indicators.note: a diverted flight is sent off its course, so these letters are sent into a new order

blocks.note: A is the top grade, as in an A-grade student
taken as written

explanation.surface: An airline passenger wonders where their premium flight has been rerouted to.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a diverted plane lands at an unplanned airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: An airfield is an area where aircraft take off and land, exactly where a diverted plane ends up.

clue.text: More passionate conflict by French waters

blocks.note: war is armed conflict
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A war being fought beside the French coastline grows more intense.
explanation.definitionFit: Warm can describe feelings that are ardent or enthusiastic, so the comparative means more ardent.

clue.text: Correct, about basics ultimately, do well

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of the preceding word is taken
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: proper means correct or fitting
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Advice that getting the fundamentals right is how you succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to flourish or thrive, especially financially.

clue.text: Look closely at initially suspicious container

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
a can is a tin container

explanation.surface: A security officer inspects a suspect package.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine something carefully, point by point.

clue.text: NI girls try dancing in exciting way

indicators.note: dancers move about and change places, so these letters swap around

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Northern Irish girls have a go at dancing in a thrilling fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirring performance rouses emotion, so the adverb means in a rousing manner.

clue.text: Ensure person being funded is seen round Dubai on regular basis

indicators.note: a regular basis means at even intervals, so every other letter of the place name is kept
to be seen round something is to go around it, so one piece encircles the other

blocks.note: a grantee receives a grant
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A funded traveller is regularly spotted around Dubai, guaranteeing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is seen' is the link between the grant recipient and the letters it surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee is to make certain that something happens or is secured.

clue.text: Board member appalling — constant flipping nonsense!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word for drivel is read backwards

blocks.note: dire means dreadful
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rot means rubbish talk

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst at a company executive who talks constant nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swear word, but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A director sits on a company's board, so is one of its members.

clue.text: Vidi, one might say

blocks.note: surface reading: the Latin word from Caesar's 'veni, vidi, vici'
setter's reading: vidi means 'I saw', which is what someone who watched an event testifies

explanation.walkthrough: Vidi is Latin for 'I saw', so the person who might say it is someone who saw something happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who witnessed an event firsthand can testify 'I saw it'.

clue.text: Formerly worked as model with little protection

blocks.note: ex means former
a model poses for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: An ex-model who once sat for artists wearing very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exposed is open to attack or the elements, lacking shelter or cover.

clue.text: Way up at hand? To some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so a stretch of the preceding words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across these words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a route upward is close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A path is a track or route, a way to go.

clue.text: Product from earth's very fresh

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Produce from the soil is extremely fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Product from earth' looks like the whole definition, but earth's letters are fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvest is the yield or result of an effort, so it can mean a product.

clue.text: Bravo! Shout of encouragement embracing non-drinker's courage

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the cheer surrounds the next piece

blocks.note: Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet
ole is the cheer at a bullfight
TT is teetotal; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A cheer for a teetotaller showing nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve, as in 'lost his bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, bottle means nerve or daring.

clue.text: Animal, much-loved, invariably obedient?

blocks.note: a pup is a young dog or seal
a pet is a favourite

explanation.surface: A beloved animal that always does as it is told.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as figurative: someone controlled by another is likened to a puppet on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet is a person whose actions are controlled by someone else, so always compliant.

clue.text: Has idea of climbing mountain with Poles in support

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means rising from bottom to top, so the word is read upward

blocks.note: an alp is a high mountain
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A mountaineer has in mind climbing with Polish companions in support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the two magnetic poles; 'in support' just says they sit below.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to have a scheme or intention in mind for it.

clue.text: Suave, finding somewhere to rest on return before broadcasting

indicators.note: a return is a journey back, so the word is read the other way round

blocks.note: a bed is a place for resting
a programme on air is being broadcast

explanation.surface: A smooth presenter looks for a place to rest after getting back, before going on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a man who is confident, stylish and charming, much like suave.

clue.text: Allowed to include female side

indicators.note: including something means holding it inside, so the first piece wraps around the second

blocks.note: let means permitted
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Women have been admitted to a team or political faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Left names one side of something, as opposed to the right-hand side.

clue.text: Astonished from beginning, took prime position

blocks.note: the start is the beginning
to lead is to be in first place

explanation.surface: A runner is amazed to have led from the off.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means surprised or shocked suddenly, close to astonished.

clue.text: Monument you discovered in New York?

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: U is text-speak for you
New York is an example of a US state, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A famous New York monument, the Statue of Liberty, that a visitor comes across.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Statue of Liberty in New York City; here New York is the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure, often erected as a monument to someone.

clue.text: Separate, careful to avoid embarrassment, they say

indicators.note: they say points to how a word is heard, so sound rather than spelling matters

blocks.note: discreet means tactful, avoiding causing embarrassment

explanation.surface: Keeping apart and being tactful, as people advise.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually distinct and separate from others.

clue.text: One acting in relation to information given ahead of time

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that opening letter is used

blocks.note: re means concerning
gen is British slang for information
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone acts on a tip-off received in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead of time' sounds like 'in advance' but takes the head of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules in place of a monarch who is a minor or absent, acting on their behalf.
